brief.prompt: Create a close-up shot of a bicycle wheel, showing its tyre and machined rim in soft window light. Work as a digital artist using geometry, procedural materials, brushwork and compositing. No image-generation models, downloaded imagery, or source-photo pixels may be used.

agent: Codex using only Rtistree studio and hand-authored code

critique.summary: Recognisable, coherently layered wheel close-up with correct curved geometry, but currently reads as a clean technical render rather than a photograph.

issues.message: Identically outlined rectangular tread blocks look flat and stamped.
issues.suggestion: Paint bevels, vary silhouettes subtly, reduce outlines and add material wear.

issues.message: Rubber is too uniform and pristine; large-scale scuffs and small irregularities are absent.
Machining lines produce excessive regular moire and the highlight is too uniform.

critique.summary: The tyre now has a curved shaded cross-section, tread bevels respond to light, and sparse abrasions replace the excessive texture experiment. Geometry, lettering, spokes and valve are coherent. The result remains a synthetic product illustration rather than a convincing photograph.

issues.message: Tread spacing and shapes remain too uniform, and surface detail lacks the multi-scale variation of real rubber.
The lighting and environment response are simplified; the blank background and regular rim highlights reinforce a rendered appearance.
A few broad scuff marks read as deliberate brush marks rather than incidental wear.
